beats: Four of my boys' school letters used to land as one shared card, in the school's flat formal wording.
I had to read it myself and tell each boy which letter was actually his.
Now two new Postgres fields hold each letter, rewritten in that boy's own first-person voice.
His own cropped photo speaks it, with who sent it named underneath, down to the minute.
Four boys, four distinct letters — nobody needs me to sort them out anymore.
